rows.description: A child says they love an aunt's gift or a bland dish to avoid hurting her. The motive is care and belonging, and the child is learning that truth and kindness can pull in different directions.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: affection, nostalgia, hurt

rows.description: A young child says the cousin broke the glass because they expect shouting or a slap. The lie is a panic move to escape a feared consequence, not a plan to deceive.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Covering a mistake or bad marks [Actor]
rows.description: A schoolchild hides a low test score or forges a signature because shame feels bigger than the truth. Each cover-up needs another lie and grows the fear it was meant to end.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A teenager hides a friendship or phone use because past honesty led to control or ridicule. The lie says more about how safe the truth felt than about the teenager's character.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22

rows.description: A person finds out a friend or partner knew something important and stayed silent. The hurt is often as sharp as for a direct lie, because they were denied the chance to decide with full information.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young professional turns assisted work into led work, telling themselves everyone does it. It feels like harmless polish until interview questions expose what they cannot actually do.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A teenager talks up money, girlfriends or fights so the group will rank them higher. Others may roll their eyes or quietly distance themselves, which the boaster rarely notices.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A small child promises to share, clean up or not cry and means it fully in that moment. They do not yet grasp that a promise binds a later self who will feel differently.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult told about a friend's troubles feels torn between loyalty and worry. They urge the friend to seek help and involve someone qualified if there is danger, instead of carrying it alone.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A toddler with crumbs on the face says no biscuit. It is a hopeful reflex, not cunning, and the child cannot yet model what the adult already knows.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12
